stem: Ayaan needs a school bag that stays useful when empty and does not tear when books are packed. He compares strong cloth and thin paper.

parts.text: Which material better fits the purpose of this bag?

options.text: Strong cloth that can hold books without tearing.
Thin paper, because it feels light in the hand.
Either cloth or paper, because any material fits any bag.
Thin paper, because a bag must be see-through.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The bag must hold books without tearing, so strong cloth matches that purpose better than thin paper.

teacher.key_rationale: A material is chosen when its properties fit the object's purpose. A school bag that must hold books needs strength; thin paper that only feels light or looks see-through does not meet that purpose.
